newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK August M4 data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK August M4 data.

text.p: Following is a list of reactions to data showing UK M4 up a provisional s/adj 9.4 percent yr-on-yr in August.
"The annual rate of growth has moved outside the
government's monitoring range and I think these figures are of
"They certainly suggest there is precious little room left for any more interest rate cuts and I think market are right to be looking for the next rise."

"The UK money data are mixed. M4 grew a stronger than expected 0.4 percent in the year to August, but the key lending counterpart was relatively soft at 4.8 bln stg. A fall in gilt repos was a key factor and helped to disguise strong personal sector borrowing. Overall tone of the data still firm enough to keep the BOE convinced that base rates should be six percent and not 5.75. But little chance of this in the foreseeable future. Coming after the surprise jump in retail sales yesterday, market likely to be little moved with virtually no-one now even contemplating a rate cut."

"All the data now are pointing to very firm economic recovery. I think the UK will look like one of the strongest economies in the world as we go into the pre-election countdown and I think the bias in interest rate markets has to increasingly shift towards the prospect of a pre-emptive rate hike. It makes the time around the (Bank of England's) November inflation report very interesting indeed."
MARIAN BELL, ROYAL BANK OF SCOTLAND

"Stronger UK M4 monetary growth in August, even than our above-consensus forecast, continues this week's strong trend in UK data which commenced with August retail sales on Wednesday. Also forecast stronger is the CBI monthly manufacturing trends enquiry tonight."
